📄 What can IPO filings reveal when we analyze both their text and visuals at scale? Excited to share our #KDD2026 paper, “IPO-Mine: A Toolkit and Dataset for Section-Structured Analysis of Long, Multimodal IPO Documents.” IPO filings are some of the most important documents companies release before entering public markets. They describe a company’s business, financials, and risks, but they are also long, messy, and multimodal: text, tables, charts, figures, logos, maps, and more. To study these filings at scale, we introduce IPO-Mine: an open-source toolkit and dataset for analyzing IPO filings with AI. 🔑 A few highlights: - 109,000+ filings and amendments from 1994 - early 2026 - 76,000+ extracted images from filings - Section-structured text extraction for long regulatory documents - Human-annotated benchmarks for section extraction and image classification - Analysis of how disclosure has changed over time - Expert-annotated evaluation of chart quality and visual design choices One result we found especially interesting: IPO text becomes more standardized over time, while visual content becomes more structurally diverse. That creates a growing modality gap for AI systems analyzing financial disclosures. This project was a true team effort with Siddharth Lohani (co-first author), Vidhyakshaya Kannan , Nik N. , Aman Patel , Liqin Ye , Arnav H. , Rutwik Routu , Prasun Banerjee , Siddhartha (Sid) Somani , and Sudheer Chava . Paper in the comments. Today I'm the first Nepali founder to join a16z speedrun , where I'm building Vene Health . I was born in Madrahani, a small village in Nepal, and immigrated to America not knowing what a startup even was. Here is my journey: Growing up in Madrahani, my dream job was to be the guy who stood outside buses calling for passengers. Eventually, my family immigrated to America through the diversity visa. America gave my family an incredible opportunity, but it also introduced obstacles. My dad became a disabled veteran serving the US army, while my mom's autoimmune disease became increasingly severe. I found myself understanding firsthand just how frustrating and exhausting healthcare in America could be for a family. At Georgia Tech, I realized I wanted to build what I wished my family had all those years to take the burden off of families like mine. That became Vene Health . Eventually, I made the decision to drop out of Georgia Tech and build Vene full-time. It wasn't an easy decision. I was walking away from school, my job at a rising startup, and the much safer path in front of me to bet everything on this. Then Afore Capital took a bet on us, and I moved to San Francisco to go completely all in. Today, a16z speedrun is taking another bet on us. It's crazy to think that the kid from Madrahani is now here. I'm incredibly proud to represent Nepal along the way.🇳🇵 None of this happened by myself. Thanks to my co-founders building this with me: Aritra Saha and Nik N. As well as: Emily Bennett Fareed Mosavat Kayla Kavanaugh Neel Jain Vikranth Keerthipati Andrew Chen Joshua Lu Jonathan Lai Lester Chen Kenan Saleh Troy Kirwin Bella Nazzari Jordan Mazer Jordan Carver Macy Mills Jacqueline Young Tabish Gilani Joan DeGennaro And many others who believed in me, helped me, challenged me, or opened a door along the way.

FIR U S26 just crossed the finish line. FIR U is built for college dropouts who believe in themselves enough to build instead. Before they headed off, I grabbed a few of them to ask one simple question: what did you ❤️ about FIR U? Their answers say everything about what we're building here: • A real community. Shared office space, constant connection, and (in their words) "so many great people in the back" that you couldn't help but meet someone new every day. The kind of place where people are still playing chess in the office at 12 am, just because they don't want to leave. • The moments outside the work: the kayaking event in Sausalito, cooking class, dinners, and World Cup watching parties. 8 weeks later, that batch felt like a family. • World-class speakers and coaching. Founders who've actually done it came in to teach sales, founding, and everything in between. • Access to the partners and the whole FIR crew, someone to talk to anytime they had a question or just wanted to think out loud. And yes, we kept everyone very well fed. :) Shariq Hafizi Shrey Parekh Jathan Pai Ibrahim Mohsin Samvrit Rao , Arjun Bakhale Aarush Yadav , Arnav Kumar Igor Martynyuk Aryan Aladar Sachin Srikanth Farhan Chowdhury Aritra Saha Sujal Dhakal Nik N. I’m excited to be speaking at Open Data Science Conference (ODSC) West, where I’ll lead the workshop Applied Machine Learning Foundations: From Features to Real-World Decisions. We’ll explore how to build and evaluate practical tabular machine learning systems using Python, Pandas, and scikit-learn. The workshop covers feature engineering, validation, anomaly detection, model comparison, and metrics such as precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC, with a focus on turning model outputs into better decisions. Join me in San Francisco, October 27–29. Registration link in the comments. #ODSCAI #MachineLearning #ScikitLearn #DataScienceTraining #AIEducation #DellProPrecision #DellTech #NVIDIA
